Add and manage a server

› /mcp
› /mcp add fetch uvx mcp-server-fetch
› /mcp add docs npx -y mcp-remote https://mcp.example.com/mcp
› /mcp remove fetch

Use /mcp to open the server picker; space toggles the selected server. Servers persist in the config file and disabled entries retain their command.

How tools are exposed

  1. mcp_search_tools searches tool metadata across configured servers.
  2. mcp_select_tool loads the full schema for exactly one result on the next turn.
  3. mcp_features reads resources, invokes prompts, and handles argument completion for a specific server.

Selected remote tools still use ordinary dispatch, approval, cancellation, and concurrency controls. Guessed tool names are rejected until selection succeeds.

Discovery before execution

Connected servers do not place every remote schema in the model context. The model first searches compact metadata, then selects one exact tool only when it needs that capability.

InterfaceUse
mcp_search_toolsSearch capability metadata across all connected servers.
mcp_select_toolExpose one exact tool schema on the next model turn.
mcp_featuresRead resources, invoke prompts, and complete arguments for one server.

A guessed remote tool name is rejected until it has been selected. That keeps a large remote catalog from consuming context before it is useful.

Connection lifecycle

Each configured stdio server is initialized and checked independently. A failed server reports its reason and does not prevent the others from connecting. Toggling one server reloads only what changed; use the MCP picker to enable, disable, and reconnect it.

Remote tools remain normal harness tools once selected: approvals, cancellation, output limits, and keyed per-server concurrency still apply. Interrupted exchanges close the serialized server connection rather than reusing a potentially stale request.

Command and credential notes

MCP launch commands split on whitespace and run without a shell: no quoting, variable expansion, or per-server environment exists. Give a server credentials through the environment used to launch Orcacode. The UI redacts recognizable secrets in server commands where it can.

PLAN MODE

Plan mode denies all MCP tools, including newly discovered tools, by design.
